title: Portfolio Band Applied to Vending Services Program Commission
content:
The commission percentage a client earns under the Vending Services Program is lifted by a portfolio band that reads every machine the client hosts rather than the single site being accrued. The band is found by adding the machine counts on the client's vending agreements standing active or suspended on the day the statement is raised, then taking the highest ladder step whose machine count does not exceed that number, using the ladder printed against the programme of the agreement being accrued. The uplift is added to the commission percentage printed against the programme, and the sum is applied to gross machine sales after card processing has been deducted.

Agreements still proposed and agreements already closed are outside the count, and machines standing out of service are counted, since they are still placed. Where the estate changes part way through a statement period, the count taken on the statement day governs that whole statement and earlier statements are not reopened.

### What enters the count

| Standing of a vending agreement on the statement day | Its machine count enters the portfolio count |
| --- | --- |
| Active | yes |
| Suspended | yes |
| Proposed | no |
| Closed | no |

Within an agreement whose count enters, a machine standing out of service is counted with the rest, because it is still placed. The count is taken across the client's vending agreements wherever their sites stand, and not only at the site whose statement is being raised; the ladder read against that count, however, is the one printed against the programme of the agreement being accrued, not the ladder of any other agreement the client holds.

### Choosing the step (hypothetical portfolio)

Take a client whose vending agreements standing active or suspended on the statement day carry 4, 9 and 4 machines, and whose fourth agreement, standing proposed, carries 6. The portfolio count is 17, being the sum of the three that count; the proposed agreement's 6 machines stay outside it. The ladder steps standing at or below 17 machines are those of 1, 5 and 12 machines, and the highest of them is the step of 12 machines, so the uplift printed at the step of 12 machines against the programme of the agreement being accrued is the uplift added.

### Working the lifted percentage through (hypothetical figures)

Suppose the agreement being accrued is written at a programme whose commission percentage is 9.00 percent, that the uplift found at the step reached is 1.00 percent, and that the card processing charge printed against the same programme is 3.00 percent. Gross machine sales of 1000.00 stand at 970.00 once card processing of 3.00 percent has been deducted. The percentage applied to that figure is 10.00 percent, being the commission percentage of 9.00 percent together with the uplift of 1.00 percent, and the commission is 97.00. The percentages and the sales figure chosen here are illustrative and are not programme figures.
